Chapter 8: The Writer’s Voice—Finding Authenticity and Style
Let’s go a step beyond structure and perspective to something a bit more mysterious: voice. It’s that special fingerprint that sets one writer apart from another. But voice isn’t just about picking the right words or arranging sentences in a certain way. It’s really the sum of all your choices, your attitude, and the way you see the world.
If you want to write, finding and shaping your authentic voice can feel tricky, but it’s also one of the most rewarding parts of the journey.
Voice comes from a mix of things—your word choices, the rhythm of your sentences, your tone, and even your point of view. It’s colored by where you come from, what you’ve experienced, and how you interpret life around you. Some writers have voices that are bold and direct. Others sound more subtle, almost musical. The trick? Don’t try to copy anyone else. Instead, listen closely to what makes someone’s writing truly their own.
Readers with a good ear start to recognize voice by the music in the prose—the way sentences dance, the kinds of images that keep popping up, and the emotions that ripple beneath the surface. You might ask yourself, what makes this writing feel so alive? How does the writer’s personality shine through?
If you’re looking to build your own voice, here are a few practical tips:
First, read as much and as widely as you can. The more voices you encounter, the more options you’ll have for your own style.
Next, don’t be afraid to imitate writers you admire—at least at first. Try on different styles like you’d try on new clothes, then start to mix things up until you find what feels right for you.
Always, listen for authenticity. Notice when a voice rings true, or when it feels a little fake or forced.
And take time to reflect on your own sensibility. What themes pop up again and again in your writing? Are there certain images or rhythms that just feel natural to you?
Here’s something worth remembering: you can’t fake your voice, and you can’t rush it either. It grows gradually, as you keep writing, reflecting, and taking creative risks.
So, keep reading closely, and keep putting words on the page. That’s how you’ll uncover the voice that’s truly yours.
